passages.text: Then the Pharisees and Sadducees came and tested Jesus by asking Him to show them a sign from heaven.
passages.sermon: The Pharisees and Sadducees came to Jesus.\r\nThey wanted to test Jesus.\r\nThey asked Jesus to show them a sign from heaven.
passages.original: Καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ Σαδδουκαῖοι πειράζοντες ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν σημεῖον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐπιδεῖξαι αὐτοῖς

passages.text: But He replied, “When evening comes, you say, ‘The weather will be fair, for the sky is red,’ and in the morning, ‘Today it will be stormy, for the sky is red and overcast.’ You know how to interpret the appearance of the sky, but not the signs of the times.
passages.sermon:
Jesus replied to the Pharisees and Sadducees.
He spoke to them directly.
He said, “In the evening, you look at the sky.
You say, ‘The weather will be fair.’
You say this because the sky is red.
In the morning, you look at the sky again.
You say, ‘Today it will be stormy.’
You say this because the sky is red and overcast.
You know how to read the sky’s appearance.
You can tell what the weather will be.
But you cannot understand the signs of the times.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὀψίας γενομένης λέγετε Εὐδία πυρράζει γὰρ ὁ οὐρανός καὶ πρωΐ Σήμερον χειμών πυρράζει γὰρ στυγνάζων ὁ οὐρανός τὸ μὲν πρόσωπον τοῦ οὐρανοῦ γινώσκετε διακρίνειν τὰ δὲ σημεῖα τῶν καιρῶν οὐ δύνασθε

passages.text: A wicked and adulterous generation demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of Jonah.” Then He left them and went away.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees and Sadducees.
They asked Him for a sign from heaven.
He called their generation wicked and adulterous.
He said this generation demands a sign.
He said no sign will be given to it.
He said only the sign of Jonah will be given.
Then Jesus left them.
He went away.
passages.original: γενεὰ πονηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλὶς σημεῖον ἐπιζητεῖ καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ καὶ καταλιπὼν αὐτοὺς ἀπῆλθεν

passages.text: When they crossed to the other side, the disciples forgot to take bread.
passages.sermon: The disciples followed Jesus.\r\nThey crossed to the other side of the lake.\r\nThe disciples forgot to bring bread.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἰς τὸ πέραν ἐπελάθοντο ἄρτους λαβεῖν

passages.text: “Watch out!” Jesus told them. “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them.
He said, “Watch out.”
He said, “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
The Pharisees and Sadducees were religious leaders.
Their teaching and influence were dangerous, like leaven in bread.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὁρᾶτε καὶ προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων

passages.text: They discussed this among themselves and concluded, “It is because we did not bring any bread.”
passages.sermon: The disciples spoke to each other.\r\nThey talked among themselves.\r\nThey said, “We did not bring any bread.”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ διελογίζοντο ἐν ἑαυτοῖς λέγοντες Ὅτι Ἄρτους οὐκ ἐλάβομεν

passages.text: Aware of their conversation, Jesus said, “You of little faith, why are you debating among yourselves about having no bread?
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus knew what the disciples were saying.
Jesus spoke to the disciples.
Jesus said, “You have little faith.”
Jesus asked, “Why are you talking among yourselves?”
Jesus asked, “Why are you worried that you have no bread?”
passages.original: Γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Τί διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ὀλιγόπιστοι ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ἔχετε

passages.text: Do you still not understand? Do you not remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many basketfuls you gathered?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus had just heard them worry about not having bread.
Jesus asked them a question.
He said, “Do you still not understand?”
He reminded them of a past event.
He said, “Do you not remember the five loaves?”
He said, “I fed five thousand people with those loaves.”
He asked, “Do you remember how many baskets you collected afterward?”
passages.original: οὔπω νοεῖτε οὐδὲ μνημονεύετε τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους τῶν πεντακισχιλίων καὶ πόσους κοφίνους ἐλάβετε

passages.text: Or the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many basketfuls you gathered?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He reminded them of a past event.
He said, “Remember the seven loaves.”
He said, “Remember the four thousand people.”
He asked, “How many baskets did you collect?”
passages.original: οὐδὲ τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους τῶν τετρακισχιλίων καὶ πόσας σπυρίδας ἐλάβετε

passages.text: How do you not understand that I was not telling you about bread? But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “I was not talking to you about bread.
You do not understand this.
Be careful of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
passages.original: πῶς οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι οὐ περὶ ἄρτων εἶπον ὑμῖν προσέχετε δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων

passages.text: Then they understood that He was not telling them to beware of the leaven used in bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
passages.sermon:
The disciples listened to Jesus.
They thought about His words.
They realized something important.
Jesus did not warn them about leaven in bread.
He warned them about the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
The Pharisees and Sadducees were religious leaders.
Their teaching was dangerous.
Jesus wanted His disciples to be careful about their teaching.
passages.original: Τότε συνῆκαν ὅτι οὐκ εἶπεν προσέχειν ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν ἄρτων ἀλλὰ ἀπὸ τῆς διδαχῆς τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων

passages.text: When Jesus came to the region of Caesarea Philippi, He questioned His disciples: “Who do people say the Son of Man is?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus came to the region called Caesarea Philippi.
Jesus had disciples with Him.
Jesus asked His disciples a question.
Jesus said, “Who do people say the Son of Man is?”
passages.original: Ἐλθὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὰ μέρη Καισαρείας τῆς Φιλίππου ἠρώτα τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγων Τίνα λέγουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι εἶναι τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου

passages.text: They replied, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”
passages.sermon:
The disciples answered Jesus.
Some people say you are John the Baptist.
Other people say you are Elijah.
Still other people say you are Jeremiah.
Some people say you are one of the prophets.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Οἱ μὲν Ἰωάννην τὸν Βαπτιστήν ἄλλοι δὲ Ἠλίαν ἕτεροι δὲ Ἰερεμίαν ἢ ἕνα τῶν προφητῶν

passages.text: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He asked them a question.
He said, "But what about you?"
He said, "Who do you say I am?"
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτοῖς Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι

passages.text: Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
passages.sermon:
Simon Peter spoke.
Simon Peter answered Jesus.
Simon Peter said, “You are the Christ.”
You are the Son of the living God.
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος εἶπεν Σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος

passages.text: Jesus replied, “Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah! For this was not revealed to you by flesh and blood, but by My Father in heaven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Simon.
Simon was the son of Jonah.
Jesus said Simon was blessed.
Jesus said, “Simon, you did not learn this from any human being.
My Father in heaven revealed this to you.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Μακάριος εἶ Σίμων Βαριωνᾶ ὅτι σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα οὐκ ἀπεκάλυψέν σοι ἀλλ’ ὁ Πατήρ μου ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς

passages.text: And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Simon Peter.
Jesus called him Peter.
Peter means "rock."
Jesus said, "You are Peter."
Jesus said, "On this rock I will build My church."
Jesus said, "The gates of Hades will not overcome My church."
passages.original: κἀγὼ δέ σοι λέγω ὅτι σὺ εἶ Πέτρος καὶ ἐπὶ ταύτῃ τῇ πέτρᾳ οἰκοδομήσω μου τὴν ἐκκλησίαν καὶ πύλαι ᾅδου οὐ κατισχύσουσιν αὐτῆς

passages.text: I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Simon Peter.
Jesus said, "I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven."
You will have authority from God.
If you bind anything on earth, it will be bound in heaven.
If you loose anything on earth, it will be loosed in heaven.
passages.original: δώσω σοι τὰς κλεῖδας τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν καὶ ὃ ἐὰν δήσῃς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται δεδεμένον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς καὶ ὃ ἐὰν λύσῃς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται λελυμένον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς

passages.text: Then He admonished the disciples not to tell anyone that He was the Christ.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus gave them a command.
He told them not to tell anyone.
He told them not to say that He is the Christ.
passages.original: Τότε διεστείλατο τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ εἴπωσιν ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός

passages.text: From that time on Jesus began to show His disciples that He must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things at the hands of the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and that He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Christ.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus began to teach His disciples.
He told them what must happen to Him.
He said He must go to Jerusalem.
He said He would suffer many things.
The elders, chief priests, and scribes would cause His suffering.
He said He must be killed.
He said He would be raised to life on the third day.
passages.original: Ἀπὸ τότε ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς δεικνύειν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὅτι δεῖ αὐτὸν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀπελθεῖν καὶ πολλὰ παθεῖν ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ ἀρχιερέων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθῆναι

passages.text: Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him. “Far be it from You, Lord!” he said. “This shall never happen to You!”
passages.sermon:
Peter was one of Jesus’ disciples.
Peter took Jesus aside.
Peter began to rebuke Jesus.
Peter said, “Lord, may this never happen to You.”
Peter said, “This will not happen to You.”
passages.original: Καὶ προσλαβόμενος αὐτὸν ὁ Πέτρος ἤρξατο ἐπιτιμᾶν αὐτῷ λέγων Ἵλεώς σοι Κύριε οὐ μὴ ἔσται σοι τοῦτο

passages.text: But Jesus turned and said to Peter, “Get behind Me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to Me. For you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Peter.
Jesus turned to him.
Jesus said, “Get behind Me, Satan!”
Jesus called Peter a stumbling block to Him.
Jesus said Peter did not think about the things of God.
Jesus said Peter thought about the things of men.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ στραφεὶς εἶπεν τῷ Πέτρῳ Ὕπαγε ὀπίσω μου Σατανᾶ σκάνδαλον εἶ ἐμοῦ ὅτι οὐ φρονεῖς τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀλλὰ τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: Then Jesus told His disciples, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself.
He must take up his cross.
He must follow Me.”
passages.original: Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ Εἴ τις θέλει ὀπίσω μου ἐλθεῖν ἀπαρνησάσθω ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθείτω μοι

passages.text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will find it.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nJesus said, “Whoever wants to save his life will lose it.\r\nWhoever loses his life for My sake will find it.”
passages.original: ὃς γὰρ ἐὰν θέλῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ σῶσαι ἀπολέσει αὐτήν ὃς δ’ ἂν ἀπολέσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εὑρήσει αὐτήν

passages.text: What will it profit a man if he gains the whole world, yet forfeits his soul? Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus asked a question about people and their souls.
A person may gain the whole world.
If he gains the whole world but loses his soul, he gains nothing.
A person cannot give anything in exchange for his soul.
passages.original: τί γὰρ ὠφεληθήσεται ἄνθρωπος ἐὰν τὸν κόσμον ὅλον κερδήσῃ τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ζημιωθῇ ἢ τί δώσει ἄνθρωπος ἀντάλλαγμα τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ

passages.text: For the Son of Man will come in His Father’s glory with His angels, and then He will repay each one according to what he has done.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus will come again.
He will come in the glory of His Father.
He will come with His angels.
Jesus will repay each person.
He will repay each one according to what that person has done.
passages.original: μέλλει γὰρ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεσθαι ἐν τῇ δόξῃ τοῦ Πατρὸς αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ καὶ τότε ἀποδώσει ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν πρᾶξιν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Truly I tell you, some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.
Some people are standing here now.
These people will not die before something happens.
They will see the Son of Man come in His kingdom.”
passages.original: Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἰσίν τινες τῶν ὧδε ἑστώτων οἵτινες οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ αὐτοῦ
